chunks: I prayed Maghrib with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) at al-Muzdalifa. When he finished, he recited the iqamah and prayed the last Isha without praying any rak'at between the two.
Then, a year later, I prayed with him: he prayed Maghrib, then stood and performed four voluntary rak'ats, then recited the iqamah and prayed the last Isha.

Then he turned to me and said: 'O Aban! These are the five obligatory prayers. Whoever establishes them and preserves their prescribed times will meet God on the Day of Resurrection, and for him with God will be a covenant by which He will admit him into Paradise. But whoever does not pray them in their prescribed times and does not preserve them — that matter is up to Him: if He wills, He will forgive him, and if He wills, He will punish him.'

key_terms.الصَّلَوَات الْخَمْس الْمَفْرُوضَات: The five obligatory prayers — Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha; their establishment (iqamah) implies performing them correctly and on time
key_terms.الْمُزْدَلِفَة: Al-Muzdalifa — the sacred station between Mina and Arafat where pilgrims spend the night during Hajj; combining Maghrib and Isha here is a known Hajj practice
key_terms.عَهْد: Covenant — a contractual guarantee from God to admit the faithful observer into Paradise
key_terms.مَوَاقِيت: The prescribed times for each prayer; preserving them (muhafazah) means not delaying them beyond their windows

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about establishing the five daily prayers and their prescribed times?
ai.summary: Aban ibn Taghlub recounts two separate occasions when he prayed with Imam al-Sadiq (AS) at al-Muzdalifa during the Hajj pilgrimage. On the first occasion, the Imam combined Maghrib and Isha immediately; on the second, he inserted voluntary prayers between them — demonstrating that both practices are permissible at Muzdalifa. The Imam then delivered a solemn teaching on the five daily prayers: those who establish them with their prescribed times are guaranteed Paradise through a divine covenant, while those who neglect them leave themselves to divine discretion — either forgiveness or punishment.
